section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the deeper distinction between a unified garment and a separate garment, using the analogy of the body and soul to illustrate that the Sefiros of Atzilus are called "bodies" while BYA are "garments."
section.t: And the explanation of the matter
(that the Sefiros of Atzilus are called bodies and BYA are garments)
in greater depth,
will be understood by prefacing that the difference between a unified garment and a separate garment is not only whether it can be removed or not,
but rather the main point is that they differ in their essence.
For the meaning of a unified garment is that it has no independent existence of its own.
For when it has an independent existence of its own,
then even if due to various reasons it cannot be removed,
the very fact that it has an independent existence of its own makes it separate,
and the meaning of
unified garment is that its entire existence is to be a garment and vessel for that which is clothed within it21.
And this is the primary difference between a person's body and his garments,
for the garments have their own independent existence,
and therefore they cover and conceal the human body clothed within them,
but not so the body, whose entire existence is to be a garment and vessel for the soul that is clothed within it,
and therefore it does not conceal the life-force of the soul clothed within it,
for in the body it is discernible that it is alive22.
And this is also the reason that the limbs of the body automatically obey the will of the soul,
for when the will of the soul arises that some action of the body's limbs should occur, the will does not need to command the limbs to do so, but rather it is done in them automatically23,
because since the entire existence of the body is to be a vessel for the soul
(as above),
therefore the action of
(the will of)
the soul in the body is in an automatic manner24.
And similarly regarding the difference between intellect and emotions versus thought, speech, and action,
the primary difference between them is,
that thought, speech, and action have their own independent existence
(and the clothing of intellect and emotions within them is an additional matter to their existence),
and therefore they conceal the intellect and emotions that are clothed within them,
but not so intellect and emotions, whose essence is that they are vessels for the soul that is clothed within them,
and it is felt in them in a revealed way that the soul acts through them
(that the soul thinks through the power of intellect,
acts with kindness through the power of kindness, etc.)19.
And based on this, it will be understood in greater depth why the Sefiros of Atzilus are called bodies and BYA are garments,
for BYA
(even the vessels of the Sefiros of BYA)
are a yesh (something with independent existence),
but not so the Sefiros of Atzilus
(even the vessels)
are Elokus (Godliness).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the distinction between Atzilus and BYA stems from their source of emanation: Atzilus emanates from the level of "light" (or) while BYA emanates from the level of "power" (koach), which allows for the perception of independent existence.
section.t: And behold, the aforementioned distinction between Atzilus and BYA,
that Atzilus is Elokus and BYA are separate entities,
is also from the perspective of the root of their coming into being.
For the coming into being of Atzilus is from the aspect of light, and the coming into being of BYA is from the aspect of power.
And the matter is25,
that it is known in the books of the philosophers that the flow of Godliness is called shefa (influx)
(for the term shefa applies both to a physical thing, like an abundance of water26,
and also to a spiritual thing, like the flow of intellect),
but in the books of Kabbalah the term light is used.
For the reason of the philosophers who termed the flow of Godliness as shefa is that the name shefa does not describe the thing being flowed,
and therefore they termed the flow of Godliness as shefa in order not to ascribe a limited depiction to Him, blessed be He.
And among the reasons that the Kabbalists called the flow of Godliness by the name light,
even though light is a description,
is because light is always attached to its source27
and when separated, it is nullified
(not so shefa, which has existence even after it is separated from its source,
like an abundance of water, where the water that flowed has existence even after they are separated from the spring,
and likewise regarding the flow of intellect,
for the intellect that flows to the student has existence even after it is separated from the teacher),
and therefore they called the flow of Godliness by the name light to indicate that the flow is always attached to Him, blessed be He.
But according to this, it needs to be understood what is written28
"You have made the heavens and the earth with Your great power,"
for power can also endure
(a little)
time even when separated from its source,
like the power of throwing,
where the power drawn into the stone and carrying it is separate from the power of the hand,
and since the Divine life-force that brings creatures into existence and sustains them is always attached to its source,
what does it mean when it says "with Your great power"?
And the explanation is,
that in order for the creations
(the heavens and the earth)
to be in the aspect of a yesh and a separate entity,
there had to be a tzimtzum (contraction) in the Divine light that brings them into existence,
so that it would be in the manner of power,
which is separate from its source.
For although in truth even the power that brings creatures into existence is always attached to its source
[for even the creations do not have an independent existence and are constantly renewed from the Divine power that brings them into existence29,
and certainly the Divine power that brings them into existence is always attached to its source30],
nevertheless,
relative to the creations, it appears to be separate from its source31,
and through this they become a yesh and a separate entity.
And it follows that the distinction between Atzilus and BYA
(that BYA are a yesh and a separate entity, and Atzilus is the world of unity)
is from the perspective of the root of their coming into being,
according to which the coming into being of BYA is from the aspect of power,
and the coming into being of Atzilus is from the aspect of light.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in Atzilus, the bittul (self-nullification) is of the level of "supernal unity," where the emanated beings are not only without independent existence but are considered as nothing at all relative to the Emanator, because their emanation is from the aspect of light.
section.t: And behold, it is known32
that in Atzilus there is the bittul of yichuda ila'ah (supernal unity),
a bittul of being considered as nothing33.
And this means that the bittul of the emanated beings to the Emanator is not only that they have no independent existence of their own
(like the creations of BYA, which are a yesh and a separate entity),
but furthermore,
they occupy no place relative to the Emanator,
they are considered as nothing.
And this will be understood by prefacing the known34
distinction between light and shefa,
that shefa is the essence of a thing,
and therefore the flow of shefa causes a change in the one who influences,
but not so light, which is merely a radiance that is incomparable to the luminary,
and therefore light does not cause a change in the luminary.

And among the reasons that the Kabbalists called the flow of Godliness by the name light is to emphasize that the fact that He, blessed be He, brings into existence and sustains all the worlds does not cause a change in Him, blessed be He,
for the life-force of all the worlds is merely a radiance that is utterly incomparable to Him.
And this matter
(that the light is incomparable relative to the luminary)
is also felt in the light.
For since the light is attached to its source and its source is felt in it,
then the fact that it is incomparable and occupies no place relative to the source,
this is also felt in the light35.
And based on this, it will be understood that the bittul of the emanated beings to the Emanator is
(not only that they have no independent existence of their own, but also)
that they occupy no place at all,
for since the coming into being of Atzilus is from the aspect of light
(as above in section 4)
that due to its attachment to the luminary, it is felt in it
(as above)
that it occupies no place,
therefore also in the emanated beings shines the revelation of the supernal knowledge that the Essence of Ein Sof is the true reality and everything is nothing relative to Him36.
